manual_notes: The release/nightly workflows and multi-platform image tooling are substantially implemented, including tag-version validation, shared test gates, plugin-full publication, GitHub Release creation, controlled tag creation and a manual no-test nightly entrypoint. The selected scope also requires a development Compose service with the repository mounted and GF_GCFG_PATH pointing to its test configuration. The inspected dev-test Compose file runs a persistent development container and PostgreSQL but declares neither the repository mount nor that configuration environment. June and July snapshots share this gap; the exact full-scope outcome remains unresolved rather than abandoned.

sources.observed_facts: Tag check precedes shared verification; release image depends on both, uses plugin-full multiarchitecture publication, and GitHub Release depends on all gates.
GitHub App token, shared release.tag.check, existing-tag rejection and controlled annotated-tag push are wired.
Manual workflow calls reusable image publication directly with two architectures and nightly tags.
Scheduled nightly publication depends on the shared verification suite.
Demo uses read-only config, PostgreSQL health dependency, tmpfs data, initialization/mock loading then app startup.
Development service uses loads/ubuntu:24.04-npm, PostgreSQL health dependency and sleep infinity, but has no volumes/repository mount or GF_GCFG_PATH.
Earlier June snapshot has the same missing repository/config wiring, so this is not inferred only from a renamed current path.
